presentingComplaint: Daily fever for 4 weeks with drenching night sweats and 6 kg weight loss, no localising symptoms, referred after an unrevealing outpatient work-up.
history: 57-year-old man with seropositive rheumatoid arthritis on long-term prednisolone 10 mg daily plus azathioprine for 3 years (functionally immunocompromised). Four weeks of documented intermittent fever to 39 °C, predominantly evening, with soaking night sweats, anorexia and 6 kg unintentional weight loss. No cough, dysuria, diarrhoea, joint flare, headache or rash. No indwelling lines or catheters and no recent hospitalisation. Two prior GP courses of oral amoxicillin-clavulanate and later azithromycin gave no response. Lives in Pune; keeps a dog; unpasteurised milk occasionally; no recent travel abroad; no injection drug use. Examination and first-line tests in clinic (chest radiograph, urinalysis, two blood-culture sets) were unremarkable, meeting the criterion of fever >3 weeks unexplained after initial ambulatory work-up, in an immune-compromised host.
examination: Ill-appearing but not toxic, well perfused. Temperature 39.0 °C during review. No focal source: chest clear, abdomen soft with 3 cm non-tender hepatomegaly and just-palpable spleen tip, shotty axillary and cervical lymphadenopathy. No new murmur, no peripheral stigmata of endocarditis, no skin lesions, no joint effusion, fundi normal, no meningism. Cushingoid habitus from chronic steroids.
imaging: Chest radiograph normal. Contrast CT chest/abdomen/pelvis: mild hepatosplenomegaly and several sub-centimetre para-aortic and axillary nodes, no abscess, no consolidation, no valvular vegetation seen. Transthoracic echocardiogram: no vegetation, normal valves. FDG-PET/CT planned to localise occult focus; bone-marrow aspirate/biopsy and directed lymph-node sampling pending.
microbiology: Two initial and one repeat blood-culture set sterile at 5 days. Urine culture sterile. Prior antibacterial courses (amoxicillin-clavulanate, azithromycin) without response. Sputum/urine not productive of a source. TB work-up (sputum/gastric Xpert MTB/RIF, IGRA) and fungal markers (serum galactomannan, beta-D-glucan), Brucella and Bartonella serology, and PET-directed tissue for histopathology and mycobacterial/fungal culture sent.
differentialDiagnoses: Disseminated tuberculosis (occult, common PUO cause in India and in immunosuppressed hosts)
Lymphoma / occult malignancy presenting with B-symptoms
Large-vessel / giant-cell arteritis and other non-infective inflammatory causes
finalDiagnosis: Pyrexia of unknown origin (immune-compromised / neutropenic-spectrum host): fever >3 weeks, >1 week of in-hospital evaluation, no diagnosis after initial cultures, cross-sectional imaging and echocardiography; staged directed work-up in progress.
citations: Harrison's Principles of Internal Medicine 22e - Fever of Unknown Origin
IDSA - Clinical Practice Guideline for the Use of Antimicrobial Agents in Neutropenic Patients with Cancer - 2010
stewardship: In classic PUO empiric antibiotics are discouraged and antipyretics/steroids are withheld until diagnosis. In an immune-compromised host with relative neutropenia and hectic fever, guideline-concordant empiric broad-spectrum anti-pseudomonal cover (piperacillin-tazobactam, or cefepime) is started after cultures, then narrowed/stopped once the systematic work-up localises the cause. Avoid reflexive escalation to carbapenems or antifungals without MDR risk or positive fungal markers; de-escalate and discontinue if cultures stay negative and an inflammatory/neoplastic cause is confirmed. Stop the earlier ineffective oral agents (source control here is diagnostic, not surgical).
contraindications: Do not commit to prolonged empiric antibiotics in classic PUO without a documented source
Avoid empiric corticosteroid escalation before excluding TB and lymphoma
Azathioprine dose caution if allopurinol co-prescribed; review myelosuppressive polypharmacy given the low ANC
edgeCases: If ANC falls <500 or patient becomes hypotensive, reclassify and manage as febrile neutropenia / sepsis with immediate empiric anti-pseudomonal cover
Positive galactomannan/beta-D-glucan would shift toward invasive fungal disease in this immunosuppressed host
Occult disseminated TB may have paradoxically low-grade inflammatory markers; a negative smear does not exclude it
expectedMaiK: Recognise immune-compromised-host PUO (fever >3 weeks, unrevealing initial work-up) and pursue a staged, hypothesis-driven work-up (repeat cultures off antibiotics, PET/CT, directed node/marrow biopsy, TB and fungal screens) rather than empiric anti-infective escalation; give guideline-concordant empiric broad-spectrum anti-pseudomonal cover only for the immunosuppressed/neutropenic risk and de-escalate as results return.
expectedNextQuestions: Any TB contact, past TB, or unpasteurised-milk/animal (Brucella) exposure?
Full drug and immunosuppression history and current ANC trend?
Any localising clue on repeated daily examination (new murmur, node, joint, skin, temporal artery tenderness)?
Fever pattern and response to withholding antipyretics/antibiotics?
expectedInvestigations: Three separate blood-culture sets off antibiotics (prolonged incubation for fastidious organisms)
FDG-PET/CT to localise an occult inflammatory, infective or neoplastic focus
Directed lymph-node excision biopsy and bone-marrow aspirate/biopsy with histology plus mycobacterial and fungal culture
TB work-up (Xpert MTB/RIF, IGRA) and fungal markers (galactomannan, beta-D-glucan)
ESR, CRP, LDH, ferritin, HIV serology, autoimmune and vasculitis screen (ANA, ANCA), Brucella/Bartonella serology

investigations: Lymph-node and bone-marrow biopsy with culture and histology
ESR/CRP, LDH, ferritin, HIV, autoimmune/vasculitis screen

regressionAssertions: Engine must rank PUO as the leading diagnosis given fever >3 weeks unexplained after initial work-up
Must classify the host as immunocompromised and not misclassify as febrile neutropenia unless ANC <500
Differential must include disseminated TB and occult malignancy/lymphoma
Stewardship must recommend empiric broad-spectrum anti-pseudomonal cover for the immunosuppressed host with a plan to narrow/de-escalate, not carbapenem or empiric antifungal by default
Must recommend PET/CT and directed tissue biopsy as key next investigations
